newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mercosur meet to set policy on Americas-wide trade.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur meet to set policy on Americas-wide trade.

text.p: The presidents of the Mercosur trading nations will meet in Paraguay next week to consolidate the bloc's position on integration into a proposed hemisphere-wide agreement, a Brazilian official said Friday.

"The meeting in Asuncion will certainly set the agenda for the future work of Mercosur and for Mercosur's position regarding the Free Trade Agreement of the Americas (FTAA)," said Jose Botafogo Goncalves, the Foreign Ministry's general secretary of economic integration and trade.
Mercosur members Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and in particular Brazil, have resisted pressure from the United States to press ahead swiftly with the FTAA negotiations.

At a meeting of trade ministers from across the Americas in Brazil in May, Mercosur frustrated the United States by leaving the issue of how to negotiate the creation of the FTAA until until another meeting in 1998.
"The co-existence of Mercosur and the FTAA in the future means we must start working now with more intensity," Botafogo told reporters.

The June 18-19 meeting in Asuncin would also deal with ongoing negotiations with the European Union and with South American nations seeking to become associate members of Mercosur like Chile and Bolivia, Botafogo said.

Finance ministers from the four Mercosur nations will meet as well in Asuncin. They will discuss new rules introduced earlier this year by Brazil to restrict import financing, which took its fellow Mercosur members by surprise.

Botafogo said another issue the ministers might discuss was Argentina's plan to introduce a 0.5 percent tariff on imports from non-Mercosur nations which could undermine the bloc's policy of setting common external tariffs.
